core_obligations: Observe that F_x is nonzero and hence has a weakly associated prime (proof lines 685-690).
Use the minimality hypothesis to identify the support of F_x (proof lines 690-692).
Conclude that m_x is weakly associated (proof lines 693-697).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: if x lies in the support of a quasi-coherent F and is not a specialisation of another point of the support, then x is weakly associated to F; in particular generic points of irreducible components of X are weakly associated to O_X (source lines 673-683). The proof argues on the stalk: F_x is nonzero, so its weakly associated primes are nonempty, the support of F_x is the single point m_x by the minimality hypothesis, and weakly associated primes lie in the support, so m_x is weakly associated.
